# Add an API test

`core/Api.java` calls the site's API without the browser and checks what comes back. Use it when a
story is about data rather than a page ("the products list returns at least one item", "an unknown
id answers 404"), or to check fast what a page test would check slowly.

```java
@Test
@Family.Smoke
void productsListAnswers() {
    Api.site().get("/api/products")
        .expectStatus(200)
        .expectJson("items[0].name")             // the field is there, whatever its value
        .expectFasterThan(2_000);
}

@Test
void anUnknownProductIsNotFound() {
    Api.site().get("/api/products/999999").expectStatus(404);
}
```

- **The address:** `Api.site()` is the site under test (`-DbaseUrl`, as every page test); a path is
  enough. `Api.at("https://api.example.com")` for an API on another host.
- **The checks:** `expectStatus`, `expectJson(path)` (the field is there), `expectJson(path, value)`
  (a number compared as a number), `expectFasterThan(ms)`; `.value(path)` or `.json()` to read it
  yourself. A path reads `items[0].name`, `total`, `[2].id`. Each check fails saying what was asked,
  what was expected and the answer.
- **Signed in:** `.asRole("user")` sends that role's account from secrets/ (as `signInAs` does);
  `.bearer(SiteConfig.secret("apiToken"))` a token from `-DapiToken` or the environment. **Never a
  literal password or token in the code.**
- **What changes data** (`post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`) runs only against a test environment, never
  the live site, as a form that sends (forms-and-test-data.md).
- **Its family:** `@Family.Smoke` if a broken API should stop a merge first; one of your own otherwise
  (Family.java says how). Each call is a step in the test's log, and in its evidence when it fails.
- **Its time:** every call is timed, yours too: target/timings/api.csv, a call much slower than in the previous run
  or past its slow line (core/Timings.java) listed at the run's end. `-DapiBudget=1.5` fails any call over 1.5 s;
  `expectFasterThan(ms)` holds one call to a time of its own.
